subject: Re: Hosting options and PoC next steps — Starlite Health
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Reynolds <amy.reynolds@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosting options and PoC next steps — Starlite Health

Hi Amy — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can lock the right PoC mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) for your use case.

Summary from the call:
- Primary constraint: PHI + strict residency — you indicated all inference must remain inside your VPC.
- Performance target: 95th pct latency target around ~120ms for the 512-token profile, and throughput ~40 req/s during peak hours.
- Key success criteria: end-to-end latency SLO, data residency proof (audit logs), and functional parity with current on-prem models for safety filters.
- Stakeholders: Amy (ML Ops), Eng Ops mailing list, Security (you mentioned Tom from compliance), and product for evaluation.

Initial recommendation: because of the PHI/residency constraint we should plan for Private VPC deployment as the default PoC path. As a fallback (if network approvals delay), a Dedicated Redwood cluster with customer-managed network peering could be a short-term option for early functional testing. Hosted API is likely unsuitable for production PHI but could be used for a 1-week smoke test if you want a rapid proof of concept for functional checks.

Proposed minimal PoC plan (6 weeks):
- Week 0-1: Security + legal + network onboarding (Vpc peering, firewall rules).
- Week 2-3: Private deployment provisioning + baseline perf run.
- Week 4: Model tuning, KV cache warm-up, quantization profile testing (if applicable).
- Week 5-6: Acceptance testing against your success criteria; produce audit artifacts and runbook.

Action items for Amy / Starlite:
1) Confirm final list of stakeholders (names + emails) who should be on the VPC/network calls.
2) Confirm whether a partial Hosted smoke test is acceptable while we queue Private provisioning.
3) Upload any additional regulatory controls checklist or point people (e.g., Tom) so we can pre-fill the SOC/penetration test expectations.

Attachments: PoC-Checklist.xlsx (initial PoC tasks), Network-Ports-Reqs.pdf (ports & peering checklist).

If that all looks right, I’ll schedule a 30-minute network kickoff and have Ben assign a PoC engineer to run the baseline perf tests.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosting options and PoC next steps — Starlite Health

Thanks, Olga — that recap is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Starlite policy requires PHI to remain in our VPC for any production workloads. Private VPC is our preferred path.
- We can do a short Hosted smoke test (no PHI) for functional validation while networking is set up, but it must use synthetic/pseudonymized data.
- Stakeholders: Amy Reynolds (ML Ops), Tom Blake (Security & Compliance), Priya Singh (Cloud Engineering), eng-ops@starlitehealth.com.

Success criteria (explicit):
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 120ms on the 512-token template for 90% of test runs.
- Throughput: sustained 30-40 req/s during a 10-minute soak test with <1% error rate.
- Data residency: confirmation that inference logs and KV cache do not leave our VPC; provide audit log sample.
- Security: pass our baseline checklist (I attached the initial security questionnaire).

We’ll need to loop in procurement once we have the preliminary cost estimate for Private deployment. Can Ben provide a back-of-envelope committed capacity cost versus a Dedicated trial configuration?

Available for the network kickoff on Mon 11/30 10:00-10:30 PT — that works for Tom and Priya.

Amy
Amy Reynolds
Head of ML Ops | Starlite Health
amy.reynolds@starlitehealth.com

Hi Amy / Olga — looping in to confirm resourcing and cost options.

Ben here from sales ops — proposed approaches and quick cost delta: 
- Private VPC PoC (customer VPC + Redwood control plane): estimated infra setup + run costs: preliminary estimate $28k - $42k for a 6-week PoC depending on GPU class and model size. This covers provisioning, 24/7 engineer support for the run, and audit artifact generation.
- Dedicated trial (Redwood-managed VPC, isolated capacity): estimated $12k - $18k for 6 weeks; faster to stand up but requires contract addendum for PHI handling and additional peering controls.
- Hosted smoke test (no PHI, synthetic data): nominal — covered under standard trial credits.

If Starlite’s security/compliance sign-off will take time, we recommend starting the Hosted smoke test in parallel (synthetic data only) to validate integration and prompt templates. Then cut over to Private VPC for PHI-required runs.

I’ll prepare a short one-page cost summary + SOW excerpt after we align on model size and expected concurrency. Olga, assigning Monica as the primary PoC engineer — Monica, can you confirm availability to start week of 12/7 if we get network approvals?

Thanks,
Ben

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Reynolds <amy.reynolds@starlitehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@starlitehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosting options and PoC next steps — Starlite Health

Thanks all — Monica from Customer Success here. Quick notes from an execution standpoint and a slightly different operational recommendation based on similar PHI customers we've onboarded: 

- We can split the PoC into a two-track approach to reduce time-to-value:
  * Track A (Hosted smoke): 1 week, functional validation with synthetic data (no PHI). Useful for prompt tuning and integration points.
  * Track B (Private VPC): full 5-week rollout focusing on performance, auditability, and production runbooks.
- Telemetry we’ll need from Starlite: distributed tracing headers, token-level cost sampling, and a sample request payload that maps to your prod templates.
- For the network kickoff please have an infra engineer on the call; we will require the CIDR ranges, preferred peering method (VPC peering vs Transit Gateway), and a list of outbound ports (attached PDF).
- Acceptance: we’ll run the 10-minute soak and provide an artifact package: perf report, audit log extract, and a runbook.

Next steps I’ll take this week:
- Draft a 1-page PoC runbook (deliverable) for signature.
- Confirm PoC engineer availability (I’m tentatively free week of 12/7).
- Book the Mon 11/30 network slot with Olga and Starlite.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
